The equation $3x^{2} - 2y^{2} = 4$ represents a hyperbola. The normal line at the point $(2, 2)$ on the hyperbola intersects the $y$-axis at the point $P$. What are the coordinates of $P$?
corrected_content.worked_solution: Differentiating gives $6x-4y\,y'=0$, hence the tangent slope at $(2,2)$ is $3/2$. The normal slope is $-2/3$, so its equation is $y-2=-\tfrac23(x-2)$. At $x=0$, $y=2+\tfrac43=\tfrac{10}3$. Thus $P=(0,\tfrac{10}3)$.
